Tara: Heads-up — Nexus Health hit a sudden token spike in embeddings during their data import. Need a short QBR-ready incident summary and mitigation plan. :rotating_light:
Ben: saw it. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/clients/nexus/spend daily tokens ~2.1M, projection monthly ~63M if unchanged.
Iris: they shipped a full patient archive import without chunking. CS notes say default pipeline used. I'll ask for the import manifest.
Marco: immediate actions I recommend:
- enable embedding batching (batch_size=128)
- run a quick hash dedupe pre-pass
- enable temporary token-cap toggle for large imports
- demo Optimize presets in the enablement call
Ben: OpsBot generated alert: OpsBot: [budget-sentinel] NEXUS-900 threshold exceeded. today_tokens=2,134,209. Suggested: temp-throttle, notify FinOps.
Tara: For QBR we need three scenarios by EOD tomorrow: "Conservative" (throttle + dedupe + batching), "Mid" (batching + quantization non-prod), "Baseline" (no change). Include tokens, $USD, and a one-line recommendation.
FinOpsBot: Acknowledged. Will post token->USD conversions and three adoption-rate sensitivity rows (25/50/100%) by tomorrow EOD.
Iris: I'll schedule a 30-min enablement with their eng lead for tomorrow 9am PT and prep a one-pager and a short demo. Also will ask the customer to opt-in to a temporary cap: "ACCEPT THROTTLE" reply to enable.
Marco: SQL snippet for slide breakdown:
```
SELECT route, sum(tokens) tokens, sum(cost_usd) cost
FROM token_events
WHERE account_id='NEXUS-900' AND ts >= '2026-03-01'
GROUP BY route
ORDER BY tokens DESC;
```
Ben: I'll add the three projection slides to the QBR deck and include the single-line takeaway: "Bulk import drove an embeddings surge; proposed mitigations can reduce monthly token spend by ~35-60% depending on adoption."
Tara: Please capture any short customer feedback on docs or friction points during the call for the renewal risk notes. If they accept throttle and adopt Optimize within 7 days, mark risk=low, else escalate. :thumbsup:
